content.text: {"what_it_is": {"claims": [{"text": "DDG Mod (budget line item 0900) is a U.S. Navy procurement line funded in the Other Procurement, Navy account.", "citation": {"fact_id": "d30e851f547180e0"}}, {"text": "The DDG Modernization (DDG MOD) program upgrades the in-service Flight I, II, and IIA DDG-51 class guided-missile destroyers to keep the class relevant and operational through a series of Hull, Mechanical, and Electrical (HM&E) and Combat Systems improvements.", "citation": {"fact_id": "96b10799995654c3"}}, {"text": "In FY2026 the program continues DDG MOD 2.0, the next phase of combat-capability enhancements, which brings Integrated Air and Missile Defense capability to the DDG 51 class by equipping ships with the SLQ-32(V)7 Surface Electronic Warfare Improvement Program Block III, the SPY-6(V)4 Air and Missile Defense Radar with an updated AEGIS baseline, and High Efficiency Super-Capacity Chillers.", "citation": {"fact_id": "96b10799995654c3"}}, {"text": "Modernization changes are aligned with New Construction design to increase commonality and capitalize on Economic Order Quantities, with DDG MOD 2.0 upgrades planned for each ship's mid-life availability.", "citation": {"fact_id": "96b10799995654c3"}}]}, "why_it_matters": {"claims": [{"text": "The line's total FY2026 request is $997,485 thousand (about $997 million), up from $861,066 thousand (about $861 million) enacted in FY2025.", "citation": {"fact_id": "d30e851f547180e0"}}, {"text": "The FY2026 request splits into a discretionary request of $686,787 thousand (about $687 million) and a reconciliation (mandatory) request of $310,698 thousand (about $311 million).", "citation": {"fact_id": "6b2e8b7f80ece145"}}, {"text": "The $310,698 thousand reconciliation request is additional mandatory funding on top of the discretionary base, together making up the line's $997,485 thousand FY2026 total.", "citation": {"fact_id": "4d3a271efe5450dd"}}, {"text": "In FY2024 the line recorded actual obligations of $641,676 thousand (about $642 million).", "citation": {"fact_id": "369fb92f190c55e7"}}, {"text": "The program's own budget narrative states the mandatory funds augment procurement, engineering, installation, and shipboard testing to provide combat capability via modernization for the in-service DDG-51 Flight IIA fleet, with further detail provided in Sections 2002 (Shipbuilding) and 2010 (Readiness) of the Reconciliation Exhibit.", "citation": {"fact_id": "40c537dcede5a7ed"}}, {"text": "The FY2026 request was reduced by $52.913 million for Advisory and Assistance Services in alignment with Executive Order 14222, the President's Department of Government Efficiency Cost Efficiency Initiative.", "citation": {"fact_id": "40c537dcede5a7ed"}}]}, "players": {"claims": [{"text": "The program is run by the U.S. Navy, with funding drawn from the Other Procurement, Navy appropriation.", "citation": {"fact_id": "6b2e8b7f80ece145"}}, {"text": "The FY2026 submission reflects updated ship schedules, including resourcing changes for USS Halsey (DDG 97) and USS Forrest Sherman (DDG 98) and an availability shift that moves USS Sampson (DDG 102) modernization into FY2026.", "citation": {"fact_id": "96b10799995654c3"}}]}, "recent_developments": {"claims": []}}
